edits.description: Find/replace operations, applied in array order against each file's current on-disk content. All edits across the whole call succeed or none are written (atomic per call, not per-file). Prefer batching every known edit into one call rather than issuing sequential calls.

path.description: Absolute path to an existing file. View the file immediately before constructing edits against it — content may differ from what you last saw.

find.description: Exact literal text, whitespace and newlines included. Must match the file's raw bytes exactly once unless `all` is true — do not include line-number prefixes from a viewer. If the match fails or is ambiguous, widen this string with more surrounding context (a preceding/following line) rather than retrying the identical value.

replace.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the matched text. Preserve the original indentation style of the surrounding block.

all.description: Set true only when you intend to replace every occurrence in the file (e.g. renaming a variable). Leave false (default) for a targeted single change — this is your main safety rail against accidental mass edits.

dry_run.description: Set true to validate all edits and return a unified diff without writing. Use this first for batches touching more than ~3 files or ~10 edits, review the diff, then repeat the same call with dry_run false (or omitted) to commit.
